newsitem.title: UK: Moody's assigns Aa3 to Unibank unit bonds.
newsitem.headline: Moody's assigns Aa3 to Unibank unit bonds.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said on Wednesday it assigned a Aa3 rating to the mortgage bonds issued by Unikredit.
Unikredit is a mortgage credit institution 100 percent owned by Unibank, rated A1/P-1/C plus, Moody's said in a statement.

"In assigning this rating, Moody's stated that it views the credit characteristics of Unikredit's mortgage bonds to be directly linked to the creditworthiness of this institution itself, and consequently to that of its parent bank, Unibank."
Moody's added that Unikredit's lending is arranged through Unibank's branches, and it is the parent bank which assesses the creditworthiness of the mortgage borrowers.
"Unibank also provides a first loss guarantee for each mortgage loan issued by Unikredit. The mortgage portfolio consists primarily of first residential mortgage loans."

Moody's said that the Aa3 rating of Unikredit's secured mortgage bonds -- when compared to Unibank's A1 long-term debt and deposit ratings -- are boosted by their comparatively lower probability of default and especially by the smaller anticipated loss-severity should a default occur.
